A.name: Product type
A.rule: One primary type, at most two secondary. Sorted by what the person comes to do, not by industry.

B.name: Layout variant
B.rule: One variant per screen; one to three per type.

C.name: Density
C.rule: Chosen for the people who use it, not for looks.

D.name: Visual style
D.rule: One base style and at most one accent style.

E.name: Reference design system
E.rule: Where components and rules come from; never copied as a look.

conflicts.says: Spacious density loses rows on every screen; work screens used all day usually take C1 or C2.
Compact density rarely suits marketing or reading pages.
Mobile first rarely suits desktop work screens; consider G1, still responsive.

rules.rule: Colour has fixed roles: a neutral ground, one action colour and four status colours (critical, warning, success, info). No colour outside a role.
rules.check: List the tokens; count colours used outside them — zero.

rules.rule: One colour, one meaning across the product; the action colour is not a status colour.
rules.check: Compare the colour-to-meaning table between screens.

sources.name: Stroop and reverse Stroop on an interactive tabletop

rules.rule: The normal state is quiet; only what needs attention carries colour.
rules.check: The share of rows with a warm status chip on one screen stays low.

rules.rule: At most five to seven status colours per entity, and about four new colour codes to learn per screen.
Colour is never the only signal: a short word or an icon always goes with it.
rules.check: In greyscale every state is still told apart.

rules.rule: Text 4.5:1, large text and component parts 3:1, in light and dark.
About four type sizes on one scale and spacing from one scale; space between groups is clearly larger than space within them.
rules.check: Count the distinct values in the CSS.

rules.rule: One dominant element and one primary button per screen.

sources.name: Erik Kennedy — 7 rules for gorgeous UI

rules.rule: Separate with space first, a line second, a box last; no box inside a box.
The most important thing is on the first screen; long pages have headings that read alone; no scroll box inside a scrolling page.
rules.check: Position of the main element against 100vh; count nested scroll areas.

rules.rule: Compare in a table, browse independent items with pictures in cards, read in order in a list.
rules.check: Check against what the person does on the screen.

sources.name: NN/g — Data tables: four major user tasks

rules.rule: Tables: numbers right-aligned in tabular figures, text left, one unit per column, sort state visible, sticky header, empty and loading states.

checks.check: Bulk actions touch only the rows the filter shows; filtering cuts the selection in the same render.
Bulk sends only rows the server marked as allowed, and says beforehand how many are skipped and why.
With pagination, the selection bar says which page the selection is on and offers "select all N".
The table is not its own scroll box inside a scrolling page; the header sticks, the pager sticks.
Sort arrows are always visible, faintly, not only on hover.
A column holding one value in 80% or more of rows is dropped or merged; no "Open" button column when the name is a link.
Identity, status, next action and what is overdue sit on top; standing explanatory paragraphs go behind a "?".
Every alert carries the way to fix it right there.
No link leads to a refusal (403) or nothing (404); say why in words instead.
A screen does not open on an empty view while the view beside it has data.
A refusal shows a sentence from one shared table of reason codes, never a raw code or the backend's English.
Field names of errors and allowlists are read from the backend code, not guessed; "" clears a field, it is not "do not send".
An error caused by a business rule links to "Why?" explained in place; an input error does not.
Nobody types a reason code; offer sentences with the code behind them; a choice list over ten items has search.
Long create or edit forms open in a dialog or a page, never inline pushing the page down; a writing dialog ends with "Cancel", a reading one with "Close".
Open every overlay (select, popover, dialog) and confirm it has content; reading text on the page is not enough.
A select or popover opened in a dialog sits above the dialog's backdrop; every floating layer has its own z-index.
Money is not a step of a funnel; counted steps go in the funnel, money is a result line beneath.
An empty cell has distinct meanings — hidden for privacy, capped, never measured — and each says so.
No row of KPI cards repeating the numbers the chart right below already draws.
Numbers are drawn only once the main source has answered; never "0 …" while waiting.
Text and ground colours go through tokens; open dark mode and measure contrast.
No horizontal scroll at 390px; header button rows may wrap. Check 1920, 1280, 860 and 390.
No button inside a button; a long screen-reader name goes in aria-label, not in visible text.
One word, one meaning per screen; buttons with one role share one label; one way of saying "empty".
Sizes, weights and colours come from tokens; markup used on a second screen becomes a component.
Count boxed nesting before showing a page: space first, lines next, boxes last.
When a prototype exists, compare the build by measurement, not by eye.
Translucent or soft-shadow styles: measure text contrast on every layer, and states must show without colour.
Motion under 200–300 ms, transform and opacity only, honour prefers-reduced-motion.

regionNotes.media-player: Use the native <video>/<audio> element; no library here ships a player.
regionNotes.map: Use a map library (for example MapLibre or Leaflet); none of these ships one.
regionNotes.canvas: Use a canvas or diagram library (for example tldraw or React Flow); none of these ships one.
regionNotes.tree: shadcn and MUI core have no tree; MUI has one in @mui/x-tree-view, not pinned here.
regionNotes.command-palette: antd, MUI and Mantine core have no command palette; Mantine has @mantine/spotlight, not pinned here; otherwise a Dialog with a search list.
regionNotes.kanban: @dnd-kit/core 6.3.1 has had no release since 2024-12; its successor @dnd-kit/react is 0.5.0, pre-1.0. Pick knowingly.
regionNotes.calendar: Month-agenda calendars with events are not in these libraries' cores; antd Calendar comes closest.

antd.name: Ant Design 6
antd.theming: ConfigProvider theme={{ token, algorithm }}; v6 writes CSS variables.

density.C3: token.controlHeight and token.fontSize raised to the C3 values

notes: The four status colours map one to one onto antd's semantic tokens.

shadcn.name: shadcn/ui on Base UI, with TanStack Table

packages.name: shadcn
packages.role: CLI that copies components into the project

shadcn.theming: CSS variables mapped through Tailwind v4 @theme; components are edited in place.

density.C1: controls h-8, table rows h-9, text-sm
density.C2: controls h-10, table rows h-12, text-sm
density.C3: controls h-12, table rows h-14, text-base

notes: shadcn ships neutral, primary and destructive only: add --warning, --success and --info and a Badge variant for each.
Run the init with Base UI primitives (--base base-ui).

mui.name: MUI 9 (Material)
mui.theming: createTheme({ cssVariables: true, palette, shape, typography }).

density.C1: DataGrid density="compact"; components size="small" through theme defaultProps

notes: The four status colours map one to one onto palette.error, warning, success and info.

mantine.name: Mantine 9
mantine.theming: createTheme({ primaryColor, colors, defaultRadius, fontFamily, fontSizes }); writes --mantine-* variables.

map.action: primaryColor (a 10-shade tuple generated from the action colour)

notes: Mantine has no semantic status roles: assign the four status colours to colour families and use them by name everywhere.
Its primary colour wants ten shades; generate them from the action colour.
